title: Keep the screensaver up until it has been focused once
head: 751481655ba6
workflow: Opus full review, Sol boundary hunter, Opus self-check of the draft, editorial check, batch gates

leads.summary: The follow-up commit removes executable permissions from both screensaver commands
leads.consequence: In a source checkout or an omarchy dev link, direct execution of either checkout script fails with Permission denied (exit 126). A bare command searched on PATH may instead fall through to an older packaged executable, silently bypassing the review head; when nothing executable is found, the idle service launches no saver and its grace/active-signal path may cancel the cycle instead of locking. The CLI router omits the non-executable checkout commands, and test/cli still passes because its sweep visits only executable files. Restore 100755 on both scripts. This does NOT describe the built package: omarchy-dev's PKGBUILD uses install -Dm755 for every bin/ script.

leads.summary: WezTerm integration can silently drop --idle even though its launcher change merges cleanly
leads.location: bin/omarchy-launch-screensaver:63-79 (the WezTerm branch added by open PR #12808)
leads.consequence: If #12808 and this PR are integrated while retaining this PR's watchdog, idle starts with --idle at Service.qml:69 but the added WezTerm branch runs plain omarchy-screensaver. On a never-focused WezTerm screen the watchdog therefore gives up after eight polls, and Service.qml:125-139 interprets its closewindow as a dismissal and cancels the pending lock. Amend the new branch to pass the full screensaver_cmd array after --. Its separate watchdog edit conflicts and needs explicit reconciliation; do not claim the entire two-PR merge is already clean.

leads.summary: The changed test passes when every terminal branch drops --idle
leads.consequence: The grep for omarchy-screensaver --idle matches only the array assignment at launcher:12, not any terminal's -e call. The test also sources the saver and manually sets screensaver_idle=1, bypassing argument parsing. Replacing all four -e uses with plain omarchy-screensaver lets the test pass even though idle launches now use the eight-poll manual give-up and may cancel the pending lock. Add a stubbed launcher invocation checking emitted argv per supported terminal, and exercise --idle parsing via an invocation or extracted parser, not only by setting the state variable.

leads.summary: Open PR #12730 also creates screensaver-test.sh and rewrites the same focus watchdog
leads.consequence: These two independent heads both add a different file at the identical test path. Applying one after the other requires a manual add/add resolution; picking either test drops the other PR's focus regressions. Their loop and --check-focus hook also conflict. Reconcile both test bodies and define how empty activewindow should affect seen_focus before either merges after the other: #12730's classifier returns success for absent class, which, if used unchanged by this PR's screensaver_lost_focus, would falsely set seen_focus=1 without any screensaver having held focus.

leads.summary: Open PR #13475 also replaces the watchdog condition, so its panel-focus fix cannot simply be overlaid
leads.consequence: The other PR hides focus-stealing open panels before launching and adds a five-second focus grace, with a fixture asserting that grace exists. The launcher panel-hiding hunk auto-merges, but its saver watchdog and this PR's new screensaver_lost_focus branch conflict. Resolving by taking only this PR's loop drops #13475's timed grace and fails its test; resolving by taking only #13475's loop drops this PR's idle no-give-up path and fails this PR's test. Combine the guarantees and retain both fixtures if both changes are wanted.

leads.summary: Configurable screensaver-command PR #10483 conflicts with the new --idle call site
leads.consequence: #10483's alternative command replaces the hardcoded service launcher. Its version's default omarchy-launch-screensaver is called without --idle, so a naive conflict resolution that picks its new launch line reintroduces never-focused idle give-up and lock cancellation. Appending --idle to all configured commands would instead pass an undocumented flag to arbitrary user launchers; append it only for the built-in command or define/validate a custom-launcher contract. This older PR is already CONFLICTING against the current base, so it is an integration warning, not an existing cleanly merged regression.

comment:
## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

Follow-up on the [earlier review](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/12258#issuecomment-5834212012), checked at `75148165` after the [author's reply](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/12258#issuecomment-5842692099).

**Verified:** all three earlier points are resolved. The follow-up commit introduces one new problem: it drops the executable bit on both screensaver scripts. Three other open PRs also rewrite the same watchdog loop, and a fourth replaces the idle launch line.

| Earlier point | Status at `75148165` |
|---|---|
| Never-focused screensaver stays up with no bound | **Resolved.** A manual launch gives up after 8 unfocused polls. An `--idle` launch keeps waiting. |
| Code comment on the stated cause | **Resolved.** The comment now says the screensaver may not be the active window when the first poll runs. |
| Optional test improvement (`rg`, loop assertion) | **Resolved.** `require_command rg` and a positive assertion for `screensaver_lost_focus` were added. Both mutations that survived before now fail the test. |

**Verified:** the author's claims hold. Runs of the real watchdog script, with no input and a stub `hyprctl` returning a non-screensaver class unless noted:

```text
Launch                                  89b4f538 (earlier head)    75148165 (this head)
manual, never focused                   still up at 20 s           exits at ~8 s (8 polls)
--idle, never focused                   n/a                        still up at 25 s
manual or --idle, focused 3 to 12 s     n/a                        exits on focus loss (~12 s)
```

The launcher forwards `--idle` as a trailing argument after `-e` for Alacritty, Ghostty, foot and kitty (stubbed launcher runs, plus each terminal's upstream argument parsing). The idle service passes `--idle` ([`Service.qml#L69`](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/blob/751481655ba6f22b4f888a035551f9b88d4313ed/shell/plugins/services/idle/Service.qml#L69)), so the #12225 fix still holds on the idle path. A never-focused idle screensaver now stays up until the lock deadline, where the lock script closes it. Keypress dismissal and dismissal on focus loss after first focus behave as before. The branch merges cleanly into current `quattro`, where the watchdog timings and the PR's test match the PR head.

### The follow-up commit drops the executable bit on both scripts

`75148165` changes `bin/omarchy-launch-screensaver` and `bin/omarchy-screensaver` from mode `100755` to `100644` (`git diff --summary 89b4f538 75148165`). Both are `100755` on the base and on current `quattro`. The test file's mode also changed, which is harmless because the test runner invokes tests with `bash`.

**Impact:**
- **Merged into current `quattro`:** `test/shell.d/screensaver-workspace-test.sh` (added on `quattro` after this PR's base) runs `"$ROOT/bin/omarchy-launch-screensaver" force` directly and fails with `Permission denied` (exit 126). With the mode restored, the same merged tree passes.
- **Dev-linked checkouts:** PATH lookup skips a non-executable file and falls through to the packaged `/usr/bin/omarchy-launch-screensaver`, which does not know `--idle`. Testing this PR through a dev link then exercises the released scripts, not the PR's. The `omarchy` command router also skips non-executable `bin/` files (from source reading, not run).
- **Packaged installs:** unaffected, because the PKGBUILDs install every `bin/*` with `install -Dm755`.

**Suggested change:** restore the mode, for example `git add --chmod=+x bin/omarchy-launch-screensaver bin/omarchy-screensaver`, and commit.

### Other open PRs change the same watchdog and launch line

The first three PRs below replace the same `read -n1 -t 1 || ! screensaver_in_focus` condition in `bin/omarchy-screensaver` with their own focus handling. The fourth changes the idle launch line in `Service.qml`:

| PR | Overlap with this PR |
|---|---|
| #12808 (WezTerm support) | Its own 10 s launch deadline with no idle exception. Adds a WezTerm launcher branch ending in `-- omarchy-screensaver`, which does not forward `--idle`. |
| #13475 (panel dismiss) | Its own 5 s focus grace period. |
| #12730 (multi-monitor screensaver) | Its own handling of an empty active-window class (exits after 3 empty polls), plus a `--check-focus` hook. Also adds `test/shell.d/screensaver-test.sh`, the same path this PR adds. |
| #10483 (configurable screensaver command) | Replaces the idle launch line this PR changes; its default command is plain `omarchy-launch-screensaver`, without `--idle`. Already conflicting with its base. |

**Impact:** whichever of the first three PRs merges second has to reconcile the watchdog by hand. The #12808 launcher itself merges without a conflict, so the missing forwarding would not surface as one. If this PR's watchdog is kept alongside #12808's WezTerm branch as written, an idle-cycle launch in WezTerm runs without `--idle`. If that screensaver never becomes the active window, it gives up after 8 unfocused polls and the pending lock is cancelled, the #12225 failure. This follows from the code in both PRs and was not run in WezTerm. If #12808's watchdog is kept instead, its 10 s deadline applies to idle launches too. Resolving #10483's conflict with its default command as written would also drop `--idle` from idle launches.

**Suggested change:** coordinate with the other PR authors on one watchdog policy. If this PR merges first, #12808's WezTerm branch needs `"${screensaver_cmd[@]}"` like the other four terminals.

**Optional test improvement:** the `--idle` plumbing is checked only as text. The launcher grep on [line 17](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/blob/751481655ba6f22b4f888a035551f9b88d4313ed/test/shell.d/screensaver-test.sh#L17) already matches the array assignment. The test sources the watchdog and sets `screensaver_idle=1` itself, so the argument loop is never exercised. Three mutations still pass the test:
- the argument loop no longer sets `screensaver_idle`, so an idle launch that never takes focus gives up after 8 unfocused polls (consequence read from the code);
- all four terminal branches revert to `-e omarchy-screensaver`;
- the launcher never matches `--idle`.

Moving the argument parsing into a function above the `BASH_SOURCE` guard and testing that function would catch the first. On `quattro`, the stubbed launch in `screensaver-workspace-test.sh` already records the exact exec command, so a `--idle` case asserting that the command contains `-e omarchy-screensaver --idle` would catch the other two.

---

## Review information

**Test scope:** Pinned head `75148165`, compared with the earlier reviewed head `89b4f538`, the base, and a local merge into current `quattro`. Source review of the changed scripts, idle service and callers, of four open PRs that touch the same files, and of the argument handling in upstream Alacritty, Ghostty, foot and kitty source. Sandboxed runs with compositor, process and terminal commands stubbed: the PR's test on base, the earlier head, the current head and the merge; mutations of the head scripts; the launcher's exec commands for each terminal; and the watchdog under scripted focus sequences. The mode effects were checked with a sandboxed PATH-lookup probe and a run of `quattro`'s test on the merge. No live Hyprland session, terminal emulator, WezTerm, dev-linked session or idle cycle was run.

**AI process:** Opus 5.5 Medium coordination and synthesis, Opus 5.5 Xhigh technical review and final fact check, GPT 6 Sol Xhigh search for related issues, Opus 5.5 Medium editorial check.
